translations.text: For many have undertaken to set down anew an account of the things fulfilled among us,
just as those who were eyewitnesses and servants of the word from the beginning handed them down to us.
It seemed good to me also, having followed everything accurately from the beginning, to write it down for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know the truth of the teachings in which you were instructed.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both were righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances.
They had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.
And it happened, while he was serving as priest before God according to his appointed days,
According to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him to enter the Lord’s temple and offer incense.
The whole crowd of people was outside praying at the hour of the incense offering.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayers have been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great before the Lord. He must drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in years.”
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.
Look, you will be mute and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
The people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he was staying so long in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. He spoke to them with gestures and remained mute.
When the days of his service were completed, he went home.
After those days, his wife Elizabeth conceived and kept herself hidden for five months, saying,
“What a thing the Lord has done for me in these days, when he looked upon me to take away my disgrace among people!”
In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a town in Galilee named Nazareth.
To a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
And he came to her and said, “Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
She was troubled by these words and wondered in her mind what kind of greeting this might be.
And the angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
And behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever,
and his kingdom will have no end.”
And Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen to me, since I do not know a man?”

The angel answered and said to her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the one who will be born from you is holy and will be called the Son of God.
And behold, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren,
for no word from God will be powerless.”
And Mary said, “Here I am, the Lord’s servant. May it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.
In those days Mary arose and went quickly into the hill country, to a city of Judah,
and entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
And when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the child leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the child in my womb leaped for joy.
And blessed is she who believes that what the Lord has spoken to her will be fulfilled.”
And Mary said, “May my soul magnify the Lord,
and my spirit rejoiced in God my Savior,
for he has looked upon the lowly condition of his servant. For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
And his mercy is upon those who fear him, from generation to generation.
He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has brought down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly.
He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He helped his servant Israel, remembering his mercies,
as he spoke to our ancestors, to Abraham and his descendants forever.
Mary stayed with her for about three months and returned to her own home.
The time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were naming him Zechariah after his father.
His mother answered, saying, “No, he shall be called John.”
They said to her, “But there is no one in your family whose name is John.”
They made signs to his father to ask what he wished to call him.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they all marveled.
Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue was freed, and he spoke and praised God.
Fear came upon everyone who heard this and upon those who lived around them, and all these things were spoken of throughout the hill country of Judea.
All who heard these things took them to heart, saying, “What will this child become?” And the hand of the Lord was with him.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, because he has visited us and brought redemption to his people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David,
as he spoke through the mouths of his holy prophets from ancient times:
salvation from our enemies and from the hands of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our ancestors and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath he swore to our father Abraham, to grant us,
rescued from the hands of our enemies, without fear,
to serve him in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our lives.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
Because of the tender mercy of our God, through which the Sun from on high will visit us,
to shine on those who sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the paths of peace.
And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his appearance to Israel.
And in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that a census should be taken throughout the whole world.
This first census took place when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
And everyone went to be registered, each to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
to be registered together with Mary, who was betrothed to him and was pregnant.
And when they arrived there, the time came for her to give birth.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
And there were shepherds in that region staying out in the open, keeping watch over their flocks at night.
And an angel of the Lord appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were greatly afraid.
And the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people.
For today a Savior has been born to you in the city of David, who is Christ the Lord.
And this will be a sign for you: you will find a child wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”
And suddenly there was with that angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth, goodwill among people.”

And when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Come, let us go to Bethlehem and see what this thing is that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in a manger.
And they understood what had been told them about the child.
And all who heard were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these things and pondered them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
And when eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.”
And to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
And there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, and he was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
He had received assurance from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Lord’s Anointed One.
And he came into the temple by the Spirit. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what was customary under the law,
And he took him into his arms, blessed God, and said:
“Now, Lord, you are releasing your servant in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before all peoples:
a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and glory for your people Israel.”
And his father and mother were amazed at the things being said about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and as a sign that will be opposed.”
“And a sword will pass through your own soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
And Anna, a prophetess, was there, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very advanced in years, having lived with her husband for seven years after her virginity.
She was a widow about eighty-four years old. She never left the temple, but worshiped with fasting and prayer night and day.
And she came forward at that very hour, gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke about him to everyone who was waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
And the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
And his parents went to Jerusalem every year for the feast of Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast.
When they had completed the days of the feast and were returning, the child Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it.
They thought he was among their traveling companions and traveled about a day’s journey, looking for him among their neighbors and acquaintances.
And when they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem to look for him.
And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at his wisdom and his answers.
And when they saw him, they were astonished, and his mother said to him, “My child, what have you done to us? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in distress.”
And he said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
And they did not understand the words he spoke to them.
He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. His mother kept all these words in her heart.
Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, there in the wilderness.
He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
As it is also written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. The difficult places will become easy, and the rocky places will become smooth roads,
and all flesh will see the salvation of God.”
He said to the crowds who came out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath that is coming?
From now on, bear fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.”
But look, the axe already lies at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
The crowds asked him, “What, then, should we do?”
He answered and said to them, “Whoever has two garments should give one to someone who has none, and whoever has food should do likewise.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Collect nothing more than you have been instructed to collect.”
The soldiers also asked him, “And what should we do?” He said to them, “Do not extort anything from anyone, and do not falsely accuse anyone. Be content with your pay.”
While the people were waiting expectantly, and everyone was wondering in their hearts about John, “Could he be the Christ?”
he answered them all, saying, “I baptize you with water, but someone more powerful than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouses, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
With many other words of encouragement as well, he proclaimed the good news to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch, who had been rebuked by him because of Herodias, his brother’s wife, and because of all the evil things Herod had done,
added this to them all: he put John in prison.
When all the people were being baptized, and Jesus too was baptized and was praying, heaven opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove. A voice came from heaven, saying, “You are my beloved Son; I am pleased with you.”
Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began [?]. He was, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, the son of Jacob, the son of Heli, the son of Matthat,
the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai.
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodad, the son of Er,
the son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Joram, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melchi, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan,
the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He neither ate nor drank during those days, and when they were over, he was hungry.
And Satan said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written: ‘A person shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
He took him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
Satan said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been given to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
So if you fall down and worship before me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.’”
He brought him to Jerusalem, set him on the tower of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here,
for it is written: ‘He has commanded his angels concerning you, to protect you,’
and ‘They will lift you up on their hands, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus answered him, saying, “It has been said: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
When Satan had finished every temptation, he departed from him for a time.
And Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread throughout all the surrounding region.
And he taught in their synagogues and was praised by everyone.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and, as was his custom, entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day.
And they gave him the scroll of the prophet Isaiah, and he stood up to read. When he opened the scroll, he found the place where it was written:
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has indeed anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted,
to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to set the wounded free, to proclaim the Lord’s year of favor.”
And he closed the scroll, gave it to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
And he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
And everyone spoke well of him and marveled at the gracious words that came from his mouth. And they said, “Is this not Joseph’s son?”
And he said to them, “Surely you will say this proverb to me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in your own region all that we have heard you did in Capernaum.’”
And he said, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his own town.
I tell you in truth that there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were shut for three years and six months, and there was a great famine throughout the whole land.
And Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath in the land of the Sidonians.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, but only Naaman the Syrian.”
And everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger when they heard this.
And they rose up, drove him out of the town, and led him to the edge of the mountain on which their town was built, to throw him down the cliff.
But he passed through their midst and went on his way.
And he went down to Capernaum, a town of the Galileans, and taught them on the Sabbaths.
And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word had authority.
And in the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out in a loud voice,
saying, “Leave us alone! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? We know who you are: the Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked him and said, “Be silent and come out of him!” The demon threw him to the ground there in their midst and came out of him without harming him at all.
And amazement came over everyone, and they spoke to one another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he rebukes unclean spirits, and they come out!”
And news about him spread to every place throughout the surrounding region.
And he left the synagogue and entered Simon’s house.
Simon’s mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they pleaded with him on her behalf.
He stood beside her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she got up and served them.
And at sunset, all who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. He laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!” But he rebuked them and did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
And when day came, he went out and went to a deserted place. The crowds looked for him and came to him, and tried to keep him from leaving them.
And he said to them, “I must also proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities, because that is why I was sent.”
And he preached in the synagogues of the Galileans.
And it happened that, while the crowd was pressing around him and listening to the word of God, he was standing beside the Lake of Gennesaret.
And he saw two boats beside the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
He got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to take it a little way out from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night and caught nothing, but at your word we will let down the nets.”
When they did this, they enclosed so many fish that their nets began to tear.
And they signaled to their fishing partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats until they were nearly sinking.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.”
For amazement had seized him and everyone with him because of the catch of fish they had taken,
and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s fishing partners. And Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid. From now on you will catch people alive.”
And when they had brought the boat ashore, they left everything and followed him.

And it happened that, when he arrived in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
He stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be clean.” And immediately the leprosy left him.
And he commanded him to tell no one, but said, “Go, show yourself to the priest, and offer a sacrifice for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
But the report about him spread all the more, and large crowds gathered to listen and to be healed of their illnesses.
But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.

And it happened one day that he was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had gathered from all the cities of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was there to heal them.
And there were men carrying a paralyzed man on a bed, and they were trying to bring him inside and lay him before him.
When they could not find a way to bring him inside because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him through the tiles, bed and all, into the midst of the gathering before Jesus.
And when he saw their faith, he said to him, “Man, let your sins be forgiven.”
The scribes and Pharisees began reasoning, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
When Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answered them, “Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say, ‘Let your sins be forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—“I tell you, get up, take your bed, and go home.”
And immediately he stood up before everyone, took up what he had been lying on, and went home, glorifying God.
Amazement seized them all, and they glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen a new sign today.”
After this he went out from there and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.”
Leaving everything, he got up and followed him.
Levi held a great feast for him in his house, and a large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at the table with them.
The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled about him to his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “The healthy have no need of physicians, but the sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples fast often and offer prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, while yours eat and drink?”
He said to them, “Can you command the wedding guests to fast while the bridegroom is with them?”
“Days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”
He also told them a parable: “No one puts a patch from a new garment onto a worn-out garment. Otherwise, he tears the new one, and the patch from the new one does not match the old.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine bursts the old wineskins, spills out, and the wineskins are ruined.
Instead, new wine must be put into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
And no one who drinks the old wine desires the new, for he says, ‘The old is sweeter.’”
On the second Sabbath after the first, he was passing through the grainfields, and his disciples plucked heads of grain, rubbed them between their palms, and ate them.
Some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered them, “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry,
how he entered the house of God, ate the bread of the Presence, and gave it to those with him, although it was not lawful for anyone to eat it except the high priests?”
He said to them, “The Son of Man is also Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath he entered the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees watched him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find an accusation against him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to the man whose hand was withered, “Get up and come into the middle.” He got up and stood there.
Jesus said to them, “Let me ask you something: What is right on the Sabbath—to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?”
Looking around at them all angrily, he said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored like the other.
They were filled with folly and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.
And it happened in those days that he went up the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.
When day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve from among them, whom he also named apostles.
Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
and Matthew and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,
and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

And he came down with them to a level place, where there was a gathering of his disciples and a very large crowd of people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and from that region and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.
They came to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
And all the people sought to get close to him, because great power went out from him and healed everyone.
And he raised his eyes toward his disciples and said, “Blessed are you who are poor in spirit, for the kingdom of God is yours.
Blessed are those who hunger now, for they will be satisfied. Blessed are those who weep now, for they will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Be glad on that day and rejoice, for look, your reward is great in heaven. Their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
“But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your comfort.”
Woe to you who are satisfied now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
But I say to you who listen: Love your enemies; do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you; pray for those who mistreat you.
To the one who strikes your cheek, offer the other also. And from the one who takes your coat, do not withhold your shirts either.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes something from you, do not demand it back.
And as you want people to treat you, treat them in the same way.
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For sinners also love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For sinners also do the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive something back, what credit is that to you? For sinners also lend to sinners so that they may receive the same amount back.

But love your enemies, and do good to those who hate you, and lend where you do not expect to receive anything back. Your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, for he is kind to the evil and the ungrateful.
Be compassionate, just as your Father is compassionate.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not punish, and you will not be punished. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you. They will pour into your lap a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you.”
He also told them a parable: “Can a blind person lead another blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not better than his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
For there is no good tree that produces bad fruit, nor, again, a bad tree that produces good fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit. People do not gather figs from thorns or pick grapes from a bramble bush.
A good person brings forth good from the good treasure of his heart, and an evil person brings forth evil from what is evil, for his mouth speaks from the abundance of his heart.
Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?
I will show you whom everyone who comes to me, hears my words, and does them is like.
He is like a man building a house who dug deep and laid the foundation on rock. When floods arose, the river struck the house but could not shake it, because its foundation was firmly laid on rock.

But the one who hears my words and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The river struck it, and it immediately fell, and the destruction of that house was great.
When he had finished all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was severely ill and near death.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to ask him to come and save his servant.
They came to Jesus and pleaded earnestly with him, saying, ‘He is worthy for you to do this favor for him.’
“For he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us.”
Jesus went with them. When he was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying, ‘Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to enter under my roof.’
‘That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.’
‘For I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, “Go,” and he goes, and to another, “Come,” and he comes, and to my servant, “Do this,” and he does it.’
When Jesus heard this, he marveled. He turned to the crowd following him and said, ‘Truly I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.’
The messengers returned to the house and found the sick servant healed.
The next day he went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a large crowd went with him.
As he approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, who was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said, ‘Do not weep.’
He came forward and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. He said, ‘Young man, I say to you, arise!’
The dead man rose and sat up and began to speak, and he gave him back to his mother.
Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, ‘A great prophet has arisen among us,’ and, ‘God has visited his people for their good.’
This report about him spread throughout all Judea and all the surrounding regions.
And John's disciples told him about all these things.
John called two of his disciples to him and sent them to the Lord, saying, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?”
When the men came to him, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?’”
At that very hour he healed many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and granted sight to many who were blind.
He answered them, saying, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor receive the good news.
And blessed is the one who does not stumble because of me.”
And when John’s messengers had gone, he began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?”
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear splendid clothing and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.’
“Truly I tell you, among those born of women there is no prophet greater than John; but the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
And when all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they acknowledged that God was just, because they had been baptized with John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and the experts in the law rejected God's purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by him.
Now, to what shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling to one another and saying, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not weep.’
John the Baptist came neither eating nor drinking, and you said, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
And wisdom was vindicated by her children.
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat a meal with him, and he entered the Pharisee's house and reclined at the table.
And there was a woman in the city who was a sinner. When she learned that he was reclining at the table in the Pharisee’s house, she brought a flask of fine oil.
She stood behind him at his feet, weeping, and began to wet his feet with her tears. She wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the oil.
And when the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what sort of woman is touching him, for she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, saying, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said, “Say it, Teacher.” And he said:
“A certain lender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When they had nothing with which to repay him, he forgave them both. Now tell me, which of them will love him more?”
Simon said, “I think it is the one whom he forgave more.” And he said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
And turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.”
“You gave me no kiss, but this woman has not stopped kissing my feet since I came in.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed with fragrant oil.
For this reason I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, because she loved greatly. For the one who is forgiven much loves much, and the one who is forgiven little loves little.”
And he said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
And those reclining at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who forgives sins?”
And he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
After this, he traveled through towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him,
along with some women who had been healed of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s chief officer, and Susanna, and many others who provided for him from their own resources.
When a large crowd gathered, and people from town after town came to him, he spoke in a parable:
“A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled underfoot, and the birds of the sky ate it.
Some fell on rock, and as it sprouted, it withered because it had no moisture.
Some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
Some fell on good, fertile soil, grew, and produced a hundredfold harvest.” After saying this, he said, “Anyone who has ears to hear, let them hear.”
His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
And he said, “You have been given knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but for the others it is in parables, so that they may look but not see, and hear but not understand.
Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
Those beside the road are the ones who hear; then Satan comes and takes the word out of their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are the ones who receive the word with joy when they hear it, but they have no roots. They believe for a time, but in a time of testing they fall away.
What fell among the thorns represents those who hear the word but, caught up in the worries, wealth, and desires of this world, are choked and become unfruitful.
What fell on fertile soil represents those who hear the word with a good and joyful heart, receive it, and bear fruit with perseverance.
No one lights a lamp and hides it under a vessel or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a lampstand so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing concealed that will not be revealed, and nothing secret that will not become known and come to light.
So take care how you listen, for whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away from them.”
His mother and brothers came to him, but they could not reach him because of the crowd.
He was told, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to see you.”
And he said to them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”
One day he got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, “Come, let us cross to the other side of this lake.” And they set out.
While they were sailing, he fell asleep, and a windstorm swept down on the lake. The boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
They came and woke him, saying, “Master, Master, look, we are perishing!” He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters. They subsided, and there was a calm.
He said to them, “Where is your faith?” They were frightened and amazed, and said to one another, “Who can this be? He commands even the winds and the waters, and they obey him.”
They sailed to the country of the Gergesenes, which is on the other side, opposite Galilee.
When he stepped ashore, a man from the city who had demons met him. For a long time he had worn no clothes and had lived not in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, saying in a loud voice, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. It had seized him for a long time. He was bound with chains and kept in iron shackles, but he would break his bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
They begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.
There was a large herd of pigs grazing there on the mountain. They begged him to allow them to enter the pigs, and he gave them permission.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep slope into the lake and drowned.
When the swineherds saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside.
When people went out to see what had happened, they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had come out sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind. They were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been delivered.
The whole crowd from the surrounding region of the Gergesenes begged him to leave their territory, because they were overwhelmed by great fear. He got into the boat and returned.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to accompany him, but he sent him away, saying:
“Return to your home and tell everything God has done for you.” He went into the city and proclaimed everything Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the people welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
And a man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. Falling at Jesus’ feet, he begged him to come into his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was near death. As he went, the crowds pressed against him.
There was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years, whom no one had been able to heal.
She approached from behind and touched the hem of his garment, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When everyone denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the crowds are pressing in and crowding you.”
Jesus said, “Someone touched me, for I knew that power had gone out from me.”

When the woman saw that she had not remained hidden from him, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of all the people, she explained why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
He said, “Take courage, daughter. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s house and said to him, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble him any further.”
But when Jesus heard this, he answered him, “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be made well.”
And when he entered the house, he allowed no one to enter except Peter, James, John, the child’s father, and her mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her, but he said, “Do not weep, for she is not dead but asleep.”
And they laughed at him, because they knew that she had died.
And after he had put everyone outside,
he took her by the hand and called out, saying, “Child, get up!”
And her spirit returned, and she stood up immediately. And he ordered that she be given something to eat.
And her parents were amazed, but he instructed them not to tell anyone what had happened.
And he called the twelve apostles together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases.
And he sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, and no money. Do not have two tunics.
Whatever house you enter, stay there and depart from there.”
And wherever they do not welcome you, when you leave that city, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.
And they went out and traveled through the towns and villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about everything that was happening and was astonished, because some were saying
that John had risen from the dead, and some that Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the prophets of old had risen.
Herod said, “I beheaded John, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.
The apostles returned and told him everything they had done. And he took them and withdrew privately to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida.
When the crowds learned of it, they followed him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed healing.

The day began to grow late, and the twelve approached and said to him, “Send the crowd away so that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms to find lodging and food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
He said to them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy enough food for this crowd.”
For there were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of fifty.”
And they did so and had everyone sit down.
And he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
And while he was praying alone, his disciples were also with him. He asked them, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
And they answered, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others say that one of the prophets of old has risen.”
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
He sternly warned them and instructed them not to tell anyone this.
And he said, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, be treated with contempt by the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”
And he said to everyone, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow me.”
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
What does a person gain by gaining the world but losing or forfeiting himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his own glory and that of the Father and the holy angels.
But truly I tell you that some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.
About eight days after these words, he took Peter, James, and John and went up the mountain to pray.
And while he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothing changed and became dazzling white.
And behold, two men were speaking with him, who were Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was to accomplish in Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him, weighed down with sleep, awoke and saw his glory and the two men standing beside him.

And as they were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He did not know what he was saying.
And when he said this, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud and said, “This is my chosen Son. Listen to him.”
And when the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.
And on the next day, as they were coming down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
And behold, a man from the crowd cried out and said, “Master, I beg you, look at my son, for he is my only child.
And behold, a spirit strikes him, and he suddenly cries out. It beats him, makes him roll about and foam at the mouth, and scarcely leaves him, having battered him.
And I begged your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered and said, “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
And while he was approaching, the demon struck him and convulsed him.
Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the child, and gave him back to his father.

And everyone was amazed at the mighty deeds of God. And while everyone was marveling at everything he was doing, he said to his disciples, “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man is going to be handed over into human hands.”
But they did not understand this saying, and it was hidden from them so that they would not understand it. And they were afraid to ask him about that saying.
A thought arose among them about which of them might be the greatest.
When Jesus perceived the thoughts of their hearts, he took a child and stood him beside himself in their midst.
And he said to them, “Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For whoever is the least among all of you will be great.”
John answered and said, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we stopped him because he does not accompany us.”
Jesus said to them, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not your enemy is on your side.”
And as the days for him to be taken up were being fulfilled, he set his face firmly toward going to Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers ahead of him. They went and entered a village of the Samaritans to make preparations for him.
But they did not receive him, because he had set his face toward going to Jerusalem.
When the disciples James and John saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and destroy them?”
He turned and rebuked them, saying, “You do not know what spirit you belong to,
for the Son of Man did not come to destroy people’s lives, but to save them.” And they went to another village.
As they were traveling along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have resting places, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
Jesus said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Another also said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say farewell to my household.”
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them out two by two ahead of him to every town and place where he himself was about to go.
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Therefore, ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into his harvest.
Go! See, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a purse, a bag, or shoes, and do not greet anyone along the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
If a person of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; otherwise, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.
Whenever you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever they set before you,
heal the sick who are there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’
But whenever you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
‘Even the dust from your town that has clung to our feet, we shake off against you. But know this: the kingdom of God has come near.’
I tell you, it will be more bearable for the people of Sodom on that day than for that town.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, who have been exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.
Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me, and whoever listens to me listens to the one who sent me.”
The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”
He said to them, “I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.”
Look, I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and on all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you; instead, rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

At that moment Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was pleasing in your sight.”
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
Then, turning to the disciples privately, he said, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.”
I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
And look, an expert in the law stood up to test him and said, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered and said, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, wounded him, left him half dead, and went away.”
By chance, a priest was going down that same road. When he saw him, he passed by.
Likewise, a Levite came to the same place, saw him, and passed by.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came to him at that same place, and when he saw him, he had compassion.
He approached him and bandaged his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them. Then he put him on his own pack animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
The next day, as he was leaving, he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, “Take care of him, and whatever you spend on him, I will repay you when I return.”
Now which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
As they went on their way, he entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary, who came and sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was occupied with much serving. She came and stood before him and said, “Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, then, to help me.”
Jesus answered and said, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and occupied with many things.”
But few things are needed here. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.
He was praying in a certain place, and when he finished, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
He said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Our Father, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come.’”
Give us our daily bread each day.
And forgive us our sins, for we too forgive everyone who owes us, and do not lead us into temptation.
And he said to them, “Which of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread’?
For a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.
And he answers from inside and says, ‘Do not trouble me, for the doors are shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything.’
I tell you, even if he does not get up and give to him because of their friendship, nevertheless, because of his persistence, he will get up and give him whatever he needs.
And I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!”
And he was casting out a mute demon. When the demon came out, the mute man spoke, and all the people were amazed.
And some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
And others tested him and sought a sign from heaven from him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and a house divided against itself falls.
So if Satan too is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say of me, ‘He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.’
If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own house, his possessions are safe.
But if someone stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away all the armor in which he trusted and distributes his plunder.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When an unclean spirit comes out of a person, it wanders through waterless places, seeking rest. And when it does not find any, it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came out.’
And it comes and finds it cleaned and put in order.
Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and live there. And that person’s final condition becomes worse than the first.”
While he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that nursed you.”
And he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
And as the crowds gathered around him, he began to say, “This generation is an evil generation. It seeks a sign, and no sign from heaven will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will also be a sign to this generation.

The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.”
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place, but on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.
The eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light, but when your eye is bad, your body will be dark.
Therefore, be careful that the light within you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be entirely bright, as when a lamp lights you with its rays.
While he was saying this, a Pharisee invited him to eat a meal with him. He went in and reclined at the table.
When the Pharisee saw this, he was surprised that he had not first washed before the meal.
The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Fools! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
But give what is due as alms, and see, everything is clean for you.
But woe to you Pharisees! You give a tenth of mint, rue, and every herb, but you pass over justice and the love of God. You ought to have done these things without neglecting the others.
Woe to you Pharisees! You love the seats of honor in the synagogues and greetings of honor in the marketplaces.
Woe to you! You are like unmarked graves, which people walk over without knowing it.”
One of the experts in the law answered him, “Teacher, by saying these things, you insult us too.”
He said, “Woe to you experts in the law too! You load people with burdens that are hard to carry, but you yourselves do not touch those burdens with even one finger.
Woe to you! You build the tombs of the prophets, and your ancestors killed them.
So you bear witness that you approve of your ancestors’ deeds, because they killed them, and you build their tombs.
For this reason the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles, and they will kill and persecute some of them,’
so that this generation may be held accountable for the blood of all the prophets shed since the beginning of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held accountable.
Woe to you experts in the law! You hide the keys of knowledge. You do not enter yourselves, and you hinder those who are about to enter.”
As he said all this to them before all the people, they were put to shame, and the scribes and Pharisees began to act hostilely toward him and provoke him about many matters,
and to lie in wait to catch some words from his mouth so that they could speak against him.
Meanwhile, as tens of thousands of people gathered, so many that they trampled one another, he began to say to his disciples, “First of all, beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
For nothing is concealed that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not become known.
Therefore, whatever you say in the darkness will be heard in the light, and whatever you whisper into someone’s ear in the storerooms will be proclaimed from the rooftops.
But I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
Even all the hairs of your head are numbered. Do not be afraid, for you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you that everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before assemblies, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how or what you will answer, or what you will say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.
Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
He said to him, “Man, who appointed me as a judge or divider over you?”
And he said to them, “Watch out and guard yourselves against every kind of greed, for a person's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
He told them a parable, saying, “The fields of a certain rich man yielded [?].
He thought to himself, saying, ‘What shall I do? I have no place to gather my produce.’
Then he said, ‘I know what I will do: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will gather my wheat and all my goods.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your soul will be demanded of you. And the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”
He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and they have neither barns nor storehouses, yet God feeds them. How much more will he feed you, who are worth more than the birds!
Which of you, by worrying, can add one cubit to his height?
If, then, you cannot do even a small thing, why worry about the rest?
Consider the lily, how it grows: it neither toils nor spins. I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so clothes the grass, which is out in the open today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
And do not seek what you will eat or what you will drink, and do not be anxious.
For the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need them all.
But seek the kingdom of God, and these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make yourselves purses that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your hearts will also be.
Keep your belts fastened around your waists and your lamps lit.
And be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open the door for him.
Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt around his waist, have them recline at the table, and come and serve them.
And if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them like this, blessed are those servants.
But know this: if the owner of the house knew at what hour the thief was coming, he would not allow his house to be broken into.
You too must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
Peter said, “Lord, did you tell this parable for us or for everyone?”
And the Lord said, “Who is the faithful and wise steward whom his master has put in charge of his household to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the unbelievers.
The servant who knows his master’s will but does not prepare himself according to his will shall receive many blows.

But the one who does not know and does something deserving of blows shall receive few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from anyone entrusted with much, still more will be demanded.
I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already blazing!
I have a baptism to undergo, and how anxious I am until it is completed!
Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on, five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three.
Father will be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
He also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, ‘Rain is coming,’ and so it happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and so it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky and the earth, but how is it that you do not interpret this time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

When you go with your opponent before the magistrate, make an effort along the way to settle with him, lest he drag you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last small coin.
Some people came at that same time and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
He answered and said to them, “Do you think that those Galileans were greater sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered such things?”
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were more guilty than all the people living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
He also told this parable: A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
He said to the gardener, “Look, for three years I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. So cut it down. Why should it also render the ground useless?”
He answered and said, “Sir, leave it for this year too, until I dig around it and put manure on it.
Perhaps it will bear fruit; but if not, you can cut it down the following year.”
And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on Sabbath days.
And there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not look up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
He laid his hand on her, and immediately she straightened up and glorified God.

The leader of the synagogue, angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded by saying to the crowd, “There are six days on which work ought to be done. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”
The Lord answered him and said, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you untie his ox or donkey from the manger on the Sabbath and lead it away to give it water?
But this woman is a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound for these eighteen years. Should she not have been freed from those bonds on the Sabbath?”
When he said this, all who opposed him were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious deeds he was doing.
He said, “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what likeness shall I compare it?”
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.
Again he said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like yeast that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole batch was leavened.”
He went through towns and villages, teaching and making his way toward Jerusalem.
Someone said to him, “Lord, are only a few going to be saved?” And he said to them,
“Strive to enter through the narrow door, for I tell you that many will seek to enter and will not be able.

Once the master of the house has gone inside and shut the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open it for us.’ And he will answer you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from.’
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our public squares.’
And he will say, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of injustice.’
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown out.
And people will come from the east and west, from the north and south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
And behold, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.
That same day some Pharisees approached and said to him, ‘Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill you.’
And he said to them, ‘Go and tell that fox, “Look, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be made complete.”’
‘But I must go on today, tomorrow, and the following day, because a prophet cannot perish outside Jerusalem.’
‘Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who killed the prophets and stoned those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!’
‘Look, your house will be left to you. But I tell you that you will no longer see me until you say, “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”’
And it happened that when he entered the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
And there before him was a man suffering from dropsy.
Jesus responded and said to the experts in the law and the Pharisees, ‘Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?’
But they remained silent. And he took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
And he said to them, ‘Which of you, if his donkey or ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?’
And they could give him no answer to this.
He also told a parable to the invited guests, noticing how they chose the places of honor. He said to them:
‘When someone invites you to a wedding or a feast, do not recline in the place of highest honor, lest someone more distinguished than you has also been invited by him,’
‘and the one who invited both you and him comes and says to you, “Give this man your place.” Then you will begin, in shame, to take the lowest place.’

‘Instead, when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, “Friend, move up higher.” Then you will have honor before those reclining at table with you.’
‘For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.’

He also said to the host, ‘When you give a lunch or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, your neighbors, or important people, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment.’
‘Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind,’
‘and you will be blessed, because they have no means to repay you. You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.’
When one of those reclining at table heard this, he said to him, ‘Blessed is the one who will eat a meal in the kingdom of God!’
And he said to him, “A man prepared a dinner and invited many people.
At dinner time he sent his servant to call those who had been invited, saying, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
But they all began, one by one, to excuse themselves. The first said, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.’

The servant came and reported this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the squares and streets of the city, and bring the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind in here.’
The servant said, ‘Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
The master said to the servant, ‘Go out to the roads and hedges and make people come in, so that my house may be filled.'
For I tell you, none of those who were invited will taste my dinner.”
Large crowds were traveling with him, and he turned and said to them,
“If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.
For whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost to see whether he has enough to finish it?
Otherwise, when he has laid the foundation and cannot finish it, everyone who sees it will begin to mock him
and say, ‘This man began to build and could not finish.’
Or what king, going to wage war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he can, with ten thousand men, withstand the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If he cannot, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for peace.
So, in the same way, any of you who does not give up all his possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt is good, but if salt loses its flavor, how can its flavor be restored?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure heap; instead, it is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
All the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.
The Pharisees and scribes grumbled and said, “Why does this man welcome sinners and eat with them?”
He told them this parable:
“Which man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
