And when he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
And he goes home, calls his friends and neighbors together, and says to them, “Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.”
I tell you that in the same way there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman who has ten coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search diligently until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, “Rejoice with me, because I have found the coin that I lost.”
In the same way, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.
And he says, “A man had two sons.”
The younger of them says to his father, “Father, give me the share of your property that falls to me.” And he divided his possessions between them.
And not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and went to a distant country. There he squandered his possessions, living recklessly.
And when he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that country, and he began to be in need.
And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him to his farm to tend pigs.
And he longed to fill his stomach with the carob pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
And coming to his senses, he says, “How many hired workers in my father’s house have plenty of bread, while I am dying of hunger here!
I will get up and go to my father and say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you,
and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.’”
And he got up and came to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and had compassion. He rose and ran to meet him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
And the son says to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.”
The father says to his servants, “Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet.
And bring the fattened ox and slaughter it. Let us eat and rejoice,
because this son of mine was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.” And they began to rejoice.
Now his older son was in the field. As he came and approached the house, he heard the sound of music and dancing.
And calling one of the servants to him, he asked what this was.
And he says to him, “Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened ox because he has received him back safe and sound.”
He became angry and would not go in, and his father came outside and pleaded with him.
He answered his father and said, “For so many years I have served you and have never disobeyed your command, yet you never gave me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.”
“When this son of yours came, who consumed your possessions with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened ox for him.”
And he says to him, “My child, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours.”
But it was right to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and came to life; he was lost and was found.
And he says to the disciples, “There was a rich man who had a manager, and an accusation was made against him that he was squandering the man’s possessions.”
He called him and said to him, “What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your management, for you can no longer be manager.”
The manager said to himself, “What shall I do, since my master is taking the management away from me? I cannot work, and I am ashamed to beg.”
“I know what I will do so that, when I am removed from the management, people will welcome me into their homes.”
He called his master’s debtors to him one by one and said to the first, “How much do you owe my master?”
He said, “A hundred baths of oil.” He said to him, “Take your bill, sit down, and quickly write fifty.”
Then he said to another, “How much do you owe?” He said, “A hundred cors of wheat.” He said to him, “Take your bill, sit down, and write eighty.”
The master praised the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this world are shrewder in dealing with their own kind than the children of light.
“And I tell you: make friends for yourselves through unrighteous wealth, so that when it runs out, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.”
“Whoever is faithful in a little is also faithful in much, and whoever is dishonest in a little is also dishonest in much.”
“So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust you with true wealth?”
“And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?”
“No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate one and love the other, or he will honor one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.”
When the Pharisees heard all this, they scoffed at him, because they loved money.
He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is exalted before people is detestable before God.”
The Law and the Prophets were until John. Since then, the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone forces their way into it.
“It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of the Law to fall away.”
“Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”
There was a rich man who dressed in fine linen and purple and celebrated lavishly every day.
A poor man named Lazarus was laid at his gate, covered with sores.
He longed to fill his belly with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The poor man died, and the angels carried him to Abraham’s embrace. The rich man also died and was buried.
In Hades, while he was in torment, he lifted his eyes and saw Abraham far away, and Lazarus resting in his embrace.
He cried out and said, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am parched in this heat.”

Abraham said to him, “My child, remember that you already received your good things during your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise received suffering. Now he is comforted here, and you are parched there.”
“Besides all this, there is a great chasm between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross from there to us.”
He said, “Then I beg you, father, to send him to my father’s house.”
“I have five brothers there, so that he may testify to them, lest they too come to this place of torment.”
And Abraham said, “They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.”
And he said, “No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.”
And he said to him, “If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.”
He also said to his disciples, “It is impossible for occasions for sin not to come, but woe to the one through whom they come!”
It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he fell into the sea than for him to cause even one of these little ones to sin.
Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
And if he sins against you seven times and returns to you seven times, saying, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
And the Lord said, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
Which of you, having a servant who plows or tends sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, “Go and sit down at once”?
But will he not say to him, ‘Prepare something for me to eat, put on your belt, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk, and afterward you may eat and drink’?
Does he thank that servant because he carried out all the commands?
So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have done what we were obliged to do.’”
And as he was going to Jerusalem, he passed through the region between Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered a certain village, ten men with leprosy met him. They stood at a distance
and raised their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
And when he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were immediately cleansed.
One of them, when he saw that he had been healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
He fell on his face at his feet and thanked him. He was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered and said, “Were not these ten cleansed? Where, then, are the nine?
Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?”
And he said to him, “Get up and go; your faith has saved you.”
When the Pharisees asked him, “When will the kingdom of God come?” he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come in a way that can be observed.”
And they will not say, “Look, it is here!” or “There!” For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
He also said to the disciples, “Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And if they say to you, ‘Look, here he is!’ or ‘There!’ do not go after them.
For as lightning flashes beneath the sky and shines across it, so will the Son of Man be on his day.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
And just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
They were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Likewise, just as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and built.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
It will be the same on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof and has belongings inside the house must not go down to get them. Likewise, whoever is in the field must not turn back.
Remember Lot’s wife.
Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will preserve it.
I tell you, on that night there will be two in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
And if there are two grinding together, one will be taken and the other left. And if there are two in the field, one will be taken and the other left.
They answered and said to him, “Where, Lord?”
He said to them, “Where the body is, there the eagles will gather.”
He also told them a parable about how they ought always to pray and not grow weary.
He said, “There was a judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor had any regard for people.
There was also a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
For a long time he was unwilling, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor have any regard for people,
at least because this widow keeps troubling me, I will give her justice, so that she will not wear me out by continually coming and pleading with me.’”
And the Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge said.
Will God not avenge his servants who cry out to him day and night, and will he merely be patient with them?
Yes, I tell you that he will bring about justice for them quickly. Yet when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?”
He also told this parable to some who were confident in themselves that they were righteous and despised many others:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood apart and offered this prayer by himself: ‘My God, I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, unjust people, adulterers—or like this tax collector.
Instead, I fast twice a week and give a tenth of all my possessions.’
But the tax collector stood apart and would not even lift his eyes toward heaven. Instead, he beat his chest and said, ‘God, forgive me, a sinner.’
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
They were also bringing infants to him so that he might touch them. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them to himself and said, “Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.
A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery; do not murder; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honor your father and mother.”
He said, “I have kept all these from my youth.”
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “You still lack one thing: sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
When he heard this, he became sad, because he was very rich.
When Jesus saw that he was sad, he said, “How difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a rope to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Those who heard this said, “Then who can be saved?”
He said, “What is impossible for human beings is possible for God.”
Peter said, “Look, we have left everything we own and followed you.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left a house or parents or brothers or a wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times as much in this time and inherit eternal life in the world to come.”
Taking the Twelve aside, he said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.”
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles and mocked,
and they will beat him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was said.
As he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road, begging.
When he heard the crowd passing by, he asked what this was.
They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
He cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those walking ahead rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and commanded that the man be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, let my eyes be opened so that I can see.”
Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has saved you.”
Immediately he could see, and he followed him, glorifying God. When all the people saw this, they gave praise to God.
And he entered Jericho and was passing through it.
And there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
He was trying to see who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd, since he was short.
And he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore fig tree to see him, because he was going to pass that way.
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down from there, because today I must stay at your house.”
He hurried down and welcomed him joyfully.
When everyone saw this, they grumbled and said, “He has gone in to stay with a sinful man.”
Zacchaeus came and stood and said to the Lord, “Lord, look, I will give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone, I will repay four times as much.”
And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.”
For the Son of Man came to seek and save what was lost.
And while they were listening to these things, he went on to tell a parable, because he was approaching Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.
He said, “A nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then return.”
And he called his servants, gave them ten minas, and said to them, “Trade with this until I return.”
But his citizens hated him and sent messengers after him, saying, “We do not want this man to reign over us.”
And when he returned, having received the kingdom, he called the servants to whom he had given the money, so that he might know what each had gained.
The first came and said, “Lord, your mina has earned ten minas.”
And he said to him, “Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in this little matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.”
The second came and said, “Your mina has made five minas.”
And he said to him, “You too shall be over five cities.”
The other came and said, “Lord, here is your mina, which I kept wrapped in a cloth.”
I was afraid of you because you are a harsh man. You take up what you did not put down and reap what you did not sow.
And he said to him, “I will judge you by your own words, unfaithful servant. You knew that I am a harsh man: I take up what I did not put down, and I reap where I did not sow.
Why, then, did you not give my money to the bankers, so that when I came I could have collected it with interest?”
And he said to the attendants, “Take the mina from him, and take it and give it to the one who has ten minas.”
And they said to him, “Lord, he has ten minas.”
“I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and kill them before me.”
And when he had said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
And when he approached Bethphage and Bethany, near the mountain called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples and said,
“Go to the village opposite us. When you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.”
And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say this to him: ‘Its Lord needs it.’
When those who had been sent went, they found the colt standing there just as he had told them.
And while they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, ‘Why are you untying that colt?’
And they said, ‘Its Lord needs it.’
And they brought it to Jesus, threw clothes over it, and seated Jesus on it.
And as he went along, they spread their clothes on the road.
And when he was already approaching the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began joyfully praising God in a loud voice for all the mighty deeds they had seen.
And they said, ‘Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!’
And some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to him, ‘Teacher, rebuke your disciples.’
He answered and said, ‘I tell you, if they fall silent, the stones will cry out.’
And as he drew near, he saw the city, wept over it, and said:
‘If only you knew, at least on this day, what brings you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.’
‘For days will come upon you when your enemies will build a rampart around you, besiege you, and press you on every side.’

‘And they will level you to the ground, along with your children within you, and they will not leave one stone upon another anywhere within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.’
And entering the temple, he began driving out the dove sellers and the buyers, and overturned the tables of the money changers.
And he said to them, ‘It is written, “My house shall be a house of prayer,” but you have made it a den of robbers.’
And he taught them daily in the temple, while the chief priests, the scribes, and the leaders of the people sought to destroy him.
And they could not find what to do, because all the people hung on his words as they listened.
And on one of those days, while he was teaching the people there in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and the scribes came up to him with the elders.
And they said to him, ‘Tell us, by what authority do you do these things, or who gave you this authority?’
He answered and said to them, ‘I too will ask you one question, and you must tell me.’
‘Was John’s baptism from heaven or from human beings?’
And they deliberated among themselves and said:

‘If we say, “From heaven,” he will say, “Then why did you not believe him?” And if we say, “From human beings,” all the people will stone us, because they are firmly convinced that John is a prophet.’
And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began telling the people this parable: ‘A man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenant farmers, and he himself went away on a journey for a long time.’
And at the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent another servant. They beat him too, dishonored him, and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent a third. They wounded him too and threw him out.
The owner of the vineyard said, “What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.”
When the tenants saw him, they discussed it among themselves and said, “This is the heir. Let us kill him so that the inheritance will be ours.”
And they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. Now what will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
Will he not come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others? When they heard this, they said, “May it never happen!”
And he looked at them and said, “Then what does this mean that is written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
Everyone who strikes against this stone will be broken to pieces, and anyone on whom it falls it will crush.”
And the scribes and chief priests sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had told this parable against them.
Then they watched him and sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in his words and hand him over to the governor’s rule and authority.
They questioned him and said, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly and show no partiality, but teach the way of God truthfully.”
“Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
And seeing through their craftiness, he said to them:
“Show me the denarius.” And they showed it to him, and he said, “Whose image and inscription does it bear?” They answered, “Caesar’s.”
And he said to them, “Then go and give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and God what belongs to God.”
And they could not catch him in his words before the people. Amazed at his answer, they fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who denied that there was a resurrection, came forward and questioned him.
They said, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies, leaving a wife but no children, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless.
The second also took her and died childless.
The third also took her, and likewise all seven, and they left no children.
The woman also died.
Now in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as their wife.”
Jesus answered them and said, “The children of this world marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are worthy to attain that world and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
For they can no longer die, because they are equal to the angels and are children of God, since they are children of the resurrection.
But that the dead rise, Moses also revealed in the passage about the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
And God is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all are alive to him.
Some of the scribes answered and said, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
And no one dared to ask him anything more.
And he said to them, “How do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
For David himself says in the Book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’
Now if David calls him Lord, how can he be his son?”
And in the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces, the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers for show. They will receive a greater condemnation.”
And he looked and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
He also saw a poor widow put two small coins into it.
And he said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
For they all contributed to the offerings to God out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on.”
And when some were speaking about the temple, saying that it was adorned with beautiful stones and towers, he said,
“As for all these things you see, days will come when not one stone here will be left upon another that will not be torn down.”
They asked him, saying, “Teacher, when will this happen, and what will be the sign when this is about to happen?”
And he said, “Be careful not to be deceived, for many will come in my name and say, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not follow them.
And when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end will not come immediately.”
Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, and famines and massacres in various places, terrors and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before judges and kings because of my name.
And this will be an opportunity for you to bear witness.
So settle it in your hearts not to rehearse your answer beforehand.
For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or answer.
You will be betrayed even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name.
Yet not a single hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance you will gain your lives.
But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its destruction is near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those who are inside the city escape, and let those who are in the countryside not enter it.
For those are days of vengeance, when everything that has been written will be fulfilled.
But woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive among all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on earth distress among the nations at a terrifying roar like that of the sea and its turmoil.
People will faint from fear and anticipation of what is coming upon the world, for the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming with clouds, with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift your heads, because your deliverance is near.
And he told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they show their fruit, you see it and know from them that summer is near.
Likewise, when you see all these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Be on your guard, lest your hearts become weighed down with excess, drunkenness, and worldly cares, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For it will come like a trap upon everyone who lives on the face of the whole earth.
From now on, stay awake and pray at all times, so that you may be found worthy to escape all these things that are going to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
During the day he taught in the temple, and at night he went out and stayed on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.
And all the people came to him early in the morning in the temple to listen to him.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which was called Passover, drew near.
And the chief priests and scribes were seeking a way to kill him, but they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, who was called Iscariot and was one of the twelve.
He went and discussed with the chief priests, the scribes, and the leaders of the people how he might betray him to them.
They were glad and promised to give him money.
He agreed and sought an opportunity to betray him to them away from the crowd.
The day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover sacrifice had to be slaughtered.
He sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat it.”
They said, “Where do you want us to prepare it?”
He said to them, “Look, when you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters,
and say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’”
And he will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.
They went and found everything as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he reclined at the table, and the twelve apostles were with him.
He said to them, “I have greatly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.”
But I tell you that I will no longer eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
He received a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
I tell you that from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for many. Do this in remembrance of me.”
Likewise, after supper he took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.”
“But look, the hand of the one who betrays me is with me at this table.
The Son of Man goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
They began to ask one another which of them would do this.
A dispute also arose among them over which of them was to be considered the greatest.
He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.
But you must not be like that. Instead, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the leader like one who serves.
For who is greater: the one reclining at the table or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are those who stood [?] with me in my trials,
and I appoint a kingdom for you, just as my Father appointed one for me.”
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom and sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And the Lord said, “Simon, Simon, look, Satan has asked to sift you all like wheat.”
But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you turn back, strengthen your brothers.
And he said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.”
And he said to him, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know me.”
And he said to them, “When I sent you without a purse, a bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?”
And they said, “Nothing at all.” Then he said, “But now, whoever has a purse must take it, and likewise a bag. And whoever does not have a sword must sell his clothing and buy one.”
“But I tell you that this which is written must also be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted among the lawless.’ For what concerns me is coming to its fulfillment.”
And they said, “Lord, look, here are two swords.” And he said to them, “They are enough.”
And he went out and, as was his custom, went to the Mount of Olives. The disciples also followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, knelt down, and prayed,
saying, “Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me. But let not my will, but yours, be done.”
And an angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him. And he was in anguish and continued praying with still greater calmness of mind.
And his sweat flowed from him like drops of blood, falling to the ground in round beads.
And when he rose from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them asleep from sorrow.
And he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.”

While he was still speaking, a crowd appeared, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. When he approached Jesus, he kissed him, for he had given them this sign: “The one I kiss is he; seize him.”
Jesus said to him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When those who were with him saw what was happening, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike them with the sword?”
And one of them struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his right ear.
Jesus answered and said, “Allow this much.” And he reached toward the ear and healed him.
And he said to those who had come against him—the chief priests, the officers of the temple, and the elders—“Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber?”
“Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay hands on me. But this is your hour and the authority of darkness.”
And they seized him, led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed him at a distance.
When they lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat around it, Peter also sat among them.
A servant girl saw him sitting by the light, looked closely at him, and said, “This man too was among those who were with him.”
But Peter denied it and said, “Woman, I do not know him.”
A little later, someone else saw him and said, “You too are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not one of them.”
About an hour later, someone else insisted, saying, “Certainly this man was with him too, for he is a Galilean.”
Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about.” Immediately, while he was saying this, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter remembered the Lord’s words to him: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny knowing me three times.”
He went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were guarding him mocked him and beat him.
They covered his face and tortured him, and questioned him, saying, “Prophesy! Who struck you?”
They said many other blasphemous things against him.
When day came, the council of the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the scribes assembled. They brought him before their council and said, “If you are the Christ, tell us.”
He said to them, “If I tell you, you will still not believe.
And if I ask you anything, you will not answer me or release me.
But from now on, the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of the power of God.”
They all said, “Then are you the Son of God?” He said to them, “You say that I am.”
They said, “What further testimony do we need? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth.”
Then the whole assembly rose and brought him to Pilate.
They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man misleading our nation, forbidding the payment of taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is the Christ, a king.”
Pilate questioned him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You have said it.”
Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no fault in this man.”
But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning in Galilee and reaching even here.”
When Pilate heard about Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that he was under Herod’s authority, he had him taken to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had often heard about him and hoped to see some miraculous sign performed by him.
He questioned him at length, but he gave him no answer.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there and accused him vehemently.
Herod and his soldiers treated him with contempt, mocked him, dressed him in white clothing, and sent him back to Pilate.
Pilate and Herod became friends that day, for previously they had been enemies of one another.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people
and said to them, “Bring this man before me as someone who leads the people astray. Look, I have examined him before you and found no fault in this man concerning the things you accuse him of.
Neither did Herod, for I sent him to him. Indeed, he has done nothing deserving death.
I will therefore punish him and release him.”
For he was required to release one prisoner to them at each festival.
But they all shouted together, saying, “Away with him! Release Barabbas to us!”
He had been put in prison for an uprising that had taken place in the city and for murder.
Pilate began to speak again, because he wanted to release Jesus.
They shouted again, saying, “Crucify him!”
He said to them three times, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no fault in him deserving death. I will punish him and release him.”
But they insisted with loud cries, demanding that he be crucified, and their voices and those of the chief priests prevailed.
Pilate agreed to grant their request.
He released Barabbas to them, the man who had been put in prison for uprising and murder, whom they were asking for, and handed Jesus over to their will.
As they took him away, they seized a man named Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, and placed the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A large crowd of people followed him, along with women who mourned and lamented him.
Jesus turned and said to them, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
For days will come when they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never gave birth, and the breasts that never nursed.’
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’
For if they do this to green wood, what will happen to the dry?”
They also brought two other men, criminals, to be put to death with him.
When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, and they crucified the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they cast lots as they divided his clothing.
The people stood watching. The rulers, along with them, sneered at him, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ, the Son of God, the Chosen One.”
The soldiers also mocked him, coming forward and offering him vinegar.
And they said, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.”
There was an inscription written above him in Greek, Dalmatian, and Hebrew letters: “This is the king of the Jews.”
One of the criminals hanging there reviled him and said, “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us.”
The other answered, rebuking him, and said, “Do you not fear God, since you are under the same punishment?”
“We are punished justly, for we are receiving what we deserve for what we have done, but this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he said to Jesus, “Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
It was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. The sun grew dark.
And the curtain of the temple was torn down the middle.
Jesus cried out in a loud voice and said, “Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit.” After saying this, he breathed his last.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God and said, “Truly, this man was righteous.”
And all the crowds who had come and witnessed that sight and what had happened beat their breasts and returned.
All his acquaintances stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee watched these things.
And there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a man who did good and was righteous.
He had not agreed with their plan and their actions. He was from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and he himself was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
He took him down, wrapped him in a linen cloth, and laid him in a rock-hewn tomb where no one had ever been laid.
It was Friday, and the Sabbath was beginning.
The women who had come with him from Galilee followed after him. They saw the tomb and how his body was laid there.
They returned and prepared spices and oils, and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, very early at dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, and other women were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
When they went inside, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they were wondering about this, suddenly two men in shining clothes appeared beside them.
They were struck with fear and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?”
“He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was in Galilee.”
And he said, “The Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, be crucified, and rise on the third day.”
And they remembered his words.
They returned and told all these things to the eleven and to all the others.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary of James, and the others with them who told these things to the apostles.
But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Looking in, he saw only the linen cloths lying there, and went away, wondering to himself what had happened.
And that same day, two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, which was a hundred and sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
And while they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself drew near and walked with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, “What are these things you are discussing with each other as you walk, and why are you sad?”
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only one staying in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?”
He said to them, “What?” They said, “About Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deeds and words before God and all the people.
“How our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be condemned to death and crucified him.
We had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel. But besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
But some women from among us also amazed us. They went early in the morning to the tomb.
And they did not find his body. They came and said that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
Some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”
He said to them, “You foolish people, slow of heart to believe everything the prophets have spoken!
Did not the Christ have to suffer these things and enter into his glory?”
And beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them everything written about him in all the Scriptures.
As they approached the village where they were going, he acted as though he would go somewhere farther on.
But they urged him strongly, saying, “Stay with us, for it is near evening, and the day is far spent.” So he went in to stay there with them.
And as he sat at the table with them, he took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished from their sight.
They said to each other, “Were not our hearts aching within us while he spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
They got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem, where they found the eleven gathered together with those who were with them.
And they said, “The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon!”
Then they told what had happened on the road and how he had made himself known to them in the breaking of the bread.
While they were speaking about these things, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you. It is I; do not be afraid.”
But they were startled and frightened and thought they were seeing a spirit.
He said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?”
Look at my hands and my feet: it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.
After saying this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
While they still could not believe because of their joy and were amazed, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of broiled fish and a honeycomb.
He took it and ate in front of them, and gave them what was left.
He said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
And he said to them, “Thus the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.”
And repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And look, I am sending my Father’s promise upon you. But stay in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.
He led them out as far as Bethany, and lifted up his hands and blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he parted from them and was taken up into heaven.
They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
They were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God.
